builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FlyingStart: Learned Cross-Token Warm Starts for Fixed-Point Decoding in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
summary: It replaces the random-noise initialization of each token's fixed-point iteration in recurrent-depth models with a linear warm start fitted in closed form on the frozen model, reducing the number of convergence loops while leaving the iteration and stopping rule unchanged. The cost is a one-time closed-form fit plus under 5% of one loop per token at inference, with no retraining. It can fail when applied to models that need few loops to converge (the paper's own analysis states the saving grows with required loop count), and it offers nothing for standard transformer architectures.
rationale: The method is cheap and training-free but applies only to recurrent-depth language models, which are not models the reader is likely to deploy on a 24 GB GPU today.
technique: Learned linear warm starts for fixed-point decoding

claims.statement: It replaces the random-noise initialization of each token's fixed-point iteration in recurrent-depth models with a linear warm start fitted in closed form on the frozen model, reducing the number of convergence loops while leaving the iteration and stopping rule unchanged. The cost is a one-time closed-form fit plus under 5% of one loop per token at inference, with no retraining. It can fail when applied to models that need few loops to converge (the paper's own analysis states the saving grows with required loop count), and it offers nothing for standard transformer architectures.
14-19% fewer decoding layers at matched accuracy on Huginn-0125, and 16-18% higher batched throughput in two serving engines (plus 10-14% on top of self-speculative decoding).
